paper.title: Algorithm 441: Random deviates from the dipole distribution (Collected Algorithms from ACM)
paper.venue: Communications of the ACM 16(1), p. 51 (January 1973), Algorithm 441. The frame lists it as TOMS 16,1; the archive header says Communications of the ACM, Vol. 16, No. 1, January 1973, P.51.
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/441.gz (article DOI not verified by scout; ACM page not fetched)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 441.gz (Fortran DIPOLE routine, its uniform generator R11, and the test driver TOMS441_PRB with its reference output in the shar file 'res')
code.archive: sha256 bb261e7a11c7b173d6cc63e70961dff7611249b99bd1eee5bffa9ada77200fb0 (downloaded by scout 2026-11-27, 19419 bytes; the shar text decompresses to 272 lines, sha256 f44af71497b019f3aa60105d144ac6b96377dbc9f10dc402974a3cb29e9f3b56)
code.note: The archive is a shar file. Extract driver.f, src.f and res from it, build the driver with a Fortran 77 or 90 compiler, and run it with no input. The driver sets seed = 123456789 itself. The claim is one line of the driver's output: the sample mean for test 2 (A = 0.353553, B = 0.353553), which the shipped 'res' file prints as 0.110592.

field: numerics (statistics: random deviates from the dipole distribution)

claim.location: Shipped reference file 'res' inside the archive (shar text lines 207-243): the block for the second test, 'A = 0.353553', 'B = 0.353553', 'Sample size = 1000', 'Sample mean = 0.110592'. The driver prints the same block as its output.

reference.file: 441/res (the 'res' member of the shar text; decompressed text saved by scout at scratch a/60/x/441.txt)

claim.paper_value: 0.110592 (sample mean of 1000 dipole deviates, A = B = 0.353553, seed 123456789; the reference file's own printed value)
claim.metric: Sample mean of the 1000 deviates generated by DIPOLE for the second test, as printed by the driver, compared as a number
claim.determinism: stochastic, seed 123456789 (set in the driver: seed = 123456789 before the loop; the uniform generator is the integer Park-Miller style R11, so the random stream is exact)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 6 significant figures, so its rounding step is 1e-6. The deviates are single precision (real) with magnitudes up to about 300, where one unit in the last place is about 3e-5. If every sample differed by one such unit in the same direction (a worst case, from a different libm or compiler rounding the sin and cos differently), the mean of 1000 would move by about 3e-5. 5e-5 covers that worst case and nothing larger. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: three tests of 1000 deviates each.
cost.data_size: None: the driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. The archive licence is not stated; the rerun should record it.

why: The driver draws seeded samples from the dipole generator and prints their sample statistics; the mean for a fixed seed needs the algorithm to run, so it tests the code rather than a closed form, and the reference file is the authors' shipped output.
